result.note: Tests the Thoothukudi greenfield shipyard location and specifications, the VOYAGES framework, and India's shipbuilding targets and fund.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways announced a tripartite MoU with South Korea's HD KSOE for India's first mega greenfield shipyard. Where is the shipyard to be built?
questions.explain: The MoU, signed in April 2026 and announced by the MoPSW on 13 May 2026, is for a facility in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu. South Korean yards bring the high-end technology, and India brings a large workforce.
questions.source: signed a tripartite MoU with South Korea’s HD KSOE earlier in April to build a massive facility in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–South Korea greenfield shipyard agreement announced in May 2026:
items: The shipyard targets an annual capacity of 2.5 million gross tonnage.
It is the first major win for VOYAGES, a maritime framework launched during South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's state visit.
The Indian signatories were National Shipbuilding & Heavy Industries Park and Sagarmala Finance Corporation.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three statements match the story. The yard targets 2.5 million GT a year under a tripartite MoU with HD KSOE, and it is the first major outcome of the VOYAGES framework.
questions.source: The yard targets an annual capacity of 2.5 million gross tonnage (GT).

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's shipbuilding push, as reported in May 2026:
items: Target year for India to be among the world's top five shipbuilders — 2047
Corpus of the Maritime Development Fund — USD 2.9 billion
New vessels India needs by 2042, as projected by the MoPSW — 734
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The third pair is wrong because the MoPSW projects that India needs 437 new vessels by 2042, not 734. The government has also overhauled the Merchant Shipping Act and launched a Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Programme to cut contract costs.
questions.source: The MoPSW projects that India needs 437 new vessels by 2042.
